# Google Search Console

Authenticated by `GOOGLE_SEARCH_CONSOLE_CREDENTIALS`, a service account key
injected from 1Password at launch. The property is `siteUrl` in
`projects.json` under this project's `google-search-console` connection.

The API takes an OAuth access token, not the key. Mint one — it lasts an
hour, is never written to disk, and stays in a shell variable:

```bash
TOKEN=$(node -e '
  const { sign } = require("node:crypto");
  const sa = JSON.parse(process.env.GOOGLE_SEARCH_CONSOLE_CREDENTIALS);
  const b64 = (o) => Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(o)).toString("base64url");
  const now = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
  const body = b64({ alg: "RS256", typ: "JWT" }) + "." + b64({
    iss: sa.client_email, scope: "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters.readonly",
    aud: sa.token_uri, iat: now, exp: now + 600 });
  const jwt = body + "." + sign("sha256", Buffer.from(body), sa.private_key).toString("base64url");
  fetch(sa.token_uri, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({
    grant_type: "urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer", assertion: jwt }) })
    .then((r) => r.json()).then((j) => process.stdout.write(j.access_token));
')
H="Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

Read-only scope, on purpose. Confirm it worked:

```bash
curl -fsS -H "$H" https://www.googleapis.com/webmasters/v3/sites | jq -r '.siteEntry[] | "\(.siteUrl)\t\(.permissionLevel)"'
```

If the property is not in that list, the account was not added to it —
`kx guide google-search-console` says where. Nothing below will work until
it is.

## Reading — safe, use freely

`S` is the property, URL-encoded: `sc-domain:x.com` is `sc-domain%3Ax.com`,
`https://www.x.com/` is `https%3A%2F%2Fwww.x.com%2F`.

```bash
S=<encoded siteUrl>
curl -fsS -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  "https://searchconsole.googleapis.com/webmasters/v3/sites/$S/searchAnalytics/query" -d '{
    "startDate": "2026-08-01", "endDate": "2026-08-31",
    "dimensions": ["query"], "rowLimit": 25
  }' | jq -r '.rows[] | "\(.clicks)\t\(.impressions)\t\(.position|floor)\t\(.keys[0])"'
```

Change `dimensions` to `["page"]`, `["query","page"]`, `["date"]` or
`["device"]` for the other cuts. Data lags two to three days; a range that
ends today is short.

```bash
curl -fsS -H "$H" "https://www.googleapis.com/webmasters/v3/sites/$S/sitemaps"
curl -fsS -H "$H" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  "https://searchconsole.googleapis.com/v1/urlInspection/index:inspect" \
  -d '{"inspectionUrl":"https://www.x.com/page","siteUrl":"<siteUrl, not encoded>"}' \
  | jq '.inspectionResult.indexStatusResult | {verdict, coverageState, lastCrawlTime, robotsTxtState}'
```

URL inspection is limited to 2,000 calls a day per property. One page at a
time, not a crawl.

## Reading the numbers

- **Position** is an average across every impression; a page at 1 for one
  query and 40 for another shows 20. Cut by `query` before concluding.
- A **drop in clicks with impressions flat** is a title or snippet problem,
  or a competitor above. A drop in both is ranking or indexing.
- `coverageState` says why a page is out: "Discovered – currently not
  indexed" is a crawl budget or quality signal, "Excluded by noindex" is
  the page saying so. Quote it verbatim.

## Never without asking

The token is read-only, so nothing here can change the property. Submitting
a sitemap or asking for a URL to be re-indexed needs a person in the
console; say which and why.
